target_customer: Developers, designers and gamers who need a powerful Windows computer without buying hardware
problem: People need high performance computers on any device without upgrading local hardware.
business_model: subscription or hourly rental of cloud computers, at $49 per month or $0.49 per hour for the Windows model

founders.name: Mykola Minchenko
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch (Dec 2016) as co-founder and CEO; no background found.

founders.name: Ievgen Nechaiev
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder on Wikipedia; the YC page lists no founders.

competitors.name: Amazon WorkSpaces
competitors.what: Windows desktops hosted on Amazon's cloud
competitors.traction_then: Launched 2013; priced from $27 per month in three tiers

technical_complexity.rationale: Low latency streaming of GPU desktops with USB peripheral support was hard for a small team; Sixa claimed 11 milliseconds latency on its side.

defensibility.rationale: The service rented infrastructure and cloud providers or Shadow could offer similar machines.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Amazon already sold cloud desktops; no sourced evidence of acquisition or copying of Sixa.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported more than 15,000 developers joined within three months of the platform launch and a beta waitlist of thousands, which shows early interest.

brand_strength.rationale: Launch coverage by TechCrunch and VentureBeat existed but nothing about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Sixa, a Ukrainian founded cloud computer startup, finished YC in Summer 2016 and raised a 3.5 million dollar seed in December 2016 with a public launch. No news after 2016 was found and YC lists it Inactive, but no shutdown notice or post-mortem exists, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty. Strong early signups did not translate into any sourced later traction.
notes: The December 2016 seed is stated by TechCrunch, VentureBeat, PYMNTS and Interfax; Interfax names Horizon Capital and Digital Future (taken from a search summary). Wikipedia says that by July 2016 Sixa had raised more than $261,000 from Startupbootcamp Istanbul, WS Investments and YC; the December 2015 $125K seed (Seedtable) and August 2016 $300K (StartupIntros, TMT Investments) each rest on a single database and may overlap with that figure. Seedtable total is 3.63M. HQ conflicts: Wikipedia San Francisco, Kyiv Post Ukraine, CB Insights Zurich. Wikipedia founders differ from the YC page, which lists none. Amazon WorkSpaces source date is a 2016 review of a 2013 product. Cause of inactivity not public.
